channel.title: Baltic News Network - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Baltic News Network (bnn-news.com)

item.title: Slovenia's liberals begin coalition talks; populists complain of vote counting flaws - Baltic News Network
item.description: Slovenian political parties are set to rush into coalition talks after no party won a majority in parliamentary elections.

item.title: A worrying trend in Lithuania: young people neither studying nor working - Baltic News Network
item.description: In Lithuania, the number of young people who are neither studying nor working has been steadily increasing in recent years.

item.title: Warmer weather approaching Latvia with temperatures up to +15°C, but rain expected first - Baltic News Network
item.description: On Tuesday, skies will be partly cloudy, with occasional clear spells during the day. The day will pass without precipitation.

item.title: “The biggest mistake would be austerity” – MP on Latvia’s economy and the crisis - Baltic News Network
item.description: Latvia should not begin implementing austerity measures in response to the impact of the war involving Iran.

item.title: Slovenia first in EU to impose fuel rationing - Baltic News Network
item.description: Slovenia has become the first EU country to impose fuel trade restrictions to counter the fallout from US and Israeli strikes.

item.title: State Security Service issues statement on Muslim community in Latvia - Baltic News Network
item.description: So far, VDD has not identified any messages justifying terrorism within the Muslim community in Latvia, and situation is stable.

item.title: Lithuania investigates possible drone crash - Baltic News Network
item.description: Lithuanian authorities are investigating a possible drone crash after an explosion was reported in Varėna District.

item.title: Russians intensify attacks on Ukrainian positions; send their own into the "meat grinder" - Baltic News Network
item.description: The commander of the Ukrainian army has reported that the Russian army has lost about 6000 soldiers in just four days.

item.title: How much does Latvia’s President earn and save? Rinkēvičs’ declaration reveals - Baltic News Network
item.description: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs increased his non-cash savings by 72,779 euros last year, reaching a total of 251,924 euros.

item.title: CVK considers referring decision on manual vote counting to Saeima - Baltic News Network
item.description: CVK is considering approaching the Saeima with a proposal to amend legislation so that the parliament would decide on manual vote counting.
